key_insight: Knowledge distillation can turn visual quantum reinforcement learning into a compact-head learning problem, allowing shallow quantum-compatible policies to learn from frozen classical visual features instead of raw pixels.
engineering_relevance: This staged hybrid approach offers a practical path for building smaller, trainable QRL controllers for high-dimensional visual tasks without relying on brittle end-to-end quantum training.
method: Train a classical visual teacher on pixel observations.
Freeze the encoder to provide a stable feature interface.
Distil teacher policy behavior into compact classical or VQC student heads using the same representation.
evidence_signal: The pipeline was evaluated on CartPole Pixels and Acrobot Pixels, where angle-encoded VQC heads achieved near-teacher performance and amplitude-encoded heads achieved extreme compactness with greater cost.
watch_item: Amplitude encoding improves compactness but is more fragile, more sensitive to budgets, and slower in simulation, which may limit practical deployment.
paper_title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation
